title: Cross-survey DINOv2 distillation: each member's 8x8 feature map must reproduce a frozen foundation-model teacher's description of the SAME place photographed in a DIFFERENT survey (training-only; the teacher never flies)
hypothesis: Through seven experiments on this ruler the held-out 2024 photograph's usable-fix rate has never left the 7-12.5% band (exp 2: 7.0%, exp 4: 11.75%, exp 5: 12.5%, exp 6: 11.0%, exp 7: 7.5%) while everything around it moved: experiment 5 lifted the TRAINING photographs to 72-81% usable at the same held-out viewpoints and 2024 did not budge, and experiment 7's committee gate cut 2024 false fixes from 38.75% to 17% but, with coverage now 0.245 (floor 0.2), there is almost nothing left to convert. The score is 0.925 + 0.17 and the 0.925 is the whole problem: the deployed trunk, trained only on three photographs, does not produce a place description that a fourth photograph reproduces. Three in-domain surveys evidently do not teach that on their own (exp 3's agreement term was vacuous, exp 6's blends were reverted, exp 4's photometrics helped once), and every mechanism tried so far derived the representation from the three photographs themselves. This experiment imports one from outside: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 with registers (Apache-2.0, 22M parameters, library L2 rank 3, the 'largest documented effect in the scene-coordinate literature' per R-SCoRe/ACE-G) is used as a frozen TRAINING-ONLY teacher, and each committee member's 8x8 trunk feature map is trained, through a training-only projector, to match the teacher's 8x8 patch-token grid of the same position and heading in a DIFFERENT training survey (TSCM's cross term). Design-stage evidence, measured on the three TRAINING captures only (runs/_probe_exp8_dinov2.py, 300 random lattice places, teacher at 112 px, nearest-neighbour place retrieval across surveys; the 2024 capture was never opened): with the raw pixels, experiment 6's probe found a place across surveys 90-97% of the time when pixel-aligned but 7-11% under a 12 px shift and 1% under shift+rotation. DINOv2's centred patch grid finds it 95.2% aligned, 70.4% under the same 12 px shift (7-10x the pixel figure) and 22.9% under shift+rotation (23x), and the teacher's own cross-survey cosine between the same place in two surveys is 0.46-0.53 against 0.05 for different places. So the teacher's description of a place survives a change of survey AND the off-lattice shift the eval imposes, which the raw pixels do not; rotation tolerance is not in the teacher and stays the student's job (it trains under random headings, as before). The cross-survey pairing is what makes the target survey-invariant rather than merely semantic: the student sees survey A's augmented crop and must produce what the teacher says about survey B's clean crop of the same ground, so canopy, shadow direction, cars and colour pipeline, which differ between A and B, cannot help it and the shared geometry can. The student is the SAME exported model as experiment 7 (3,942,411 bytes); only the training loss changes. Two known limits are honest unknowns: whether a 0.97M-parameter two-member student can absorb enough of a 22M teacher's geometry (no published distillation result below 4M parameters), and whether the 14 m patch granularity at 112 px is right for a 128 m cell head. Cost: the teacher runs online, no cache; a ViT-S forward at 112 px is ~2.9 GFLOP, ~0.6 PFLOP per epoch of 218k views, a few tens of seconds on the L4 the loop trains on (REMOTE_TRAIN=1); measured 296 img/s on the M1 (12 min/epoch) if a run ever falls back to local training.
method: ONE change: add a training-only cross-survey feature-distillation loss. (1) model/model.py: Member exposes feature_map(x) -> [B,112,8,8] (its conv stack before global average pooling); forward() is unchanged in effect (GAP of that map). Nothing in the exported graph changes. (2) model/train.py: load DINOv2 ViT-S/14-reg via torch.hub (frozen, eval, no grad; fp16 autocast on CUDA). Per mini-batch, besides each member's own augmented crop of its survey, cut the SAME position and heading from a different training capture (partner = (cap + randint(1, n_caps)) % n_caps), feed the clean partner crop to the teacher at 112 px (ImageNet-normalised) and take its 64 patch tokens as an [B,384,8,8] grid, batch-centred and L2-normalised per position. Each member gets a training-only projector (1x1 conv 112->512, ReLU, 1x1 conv 512->384, DisCo-wide) on its feature map of the AUGMENTED own-survey crop; loss_k += DISTILL_WEIGHT * mean over B x 8 x 8 of (1 - cosine(projected student, teacher target)). DISTILL_WEIGHT = 5.0. Projectors are optimised with the model and discarded at export. The committee, paired-survey interleave, photometric augmentation, tent targets, offset targets, schedule and views per epoch are unchanged.
expected_outcome: Primary (held-out truedop_2024): 1.096 -> predicted 0.90-1.03, and for the first time in this era through usable_fix_rate: 7.5% -> 12-20%, with false_fix_rate 17% -> 10-16% (frames the two members now agree on are enriched for frames where survey-invariant geometry names the cell). 2024 coverage rises from 0.245 to 0.30-0.45 as the members, trained toward one external description, agree more often; the 0.2 FAIL floor is therefore not expected to bind, and if coverage FALLS the mechanism did not transfer. 2024 median error among confident frames (1,342 m) should drop below 600 m. train_capture_diagnostics (bb_dop20 / truedop_2022 / truedop_2023 = 0.833 / 0.845 / 0.703 on exp 7, usable 22 / 18 / 32%) are predicted to IMPROVE to 0.55-0.75 each (usable 30-45%), because a semantic target is also an easier fit than 2,970 classes from scratch; the evidence that matters is the gap between those three numbers and the 2024 score narrowing, not the training numbers alone. Mechanical checks that must hold or the mechanism did not bite: the logged per-member student-teacher cosine (centred, mean over positions) ends above 0.55 for both members (the teacher's own cross-survey floor is 0.46-0.53, so matching the cross-survey target at that level means the student has reached the teacher's invariant part); the logged distillation loss falls monotonically; exported bytes read exactly 3,942,411 and host latency ~2 ms (the deployed graph is untouched); per-member top1 and agree_rate end at or above exp 7's 0.35 / 0.35. Decision rules: (a) 2024 usable up by >= 4 points with false fix not rising -> supported; the next experiment raises the teacher's granularity (224 px input, 16x16 tokens pooled to 8x8, or a stride-8 tap) or widens the student. (b) student-teacher cosine > 0.55 but 2024 usable flat (<= 10%) -> the teacher's 14 m geometry does not carry place identity through this student; the next move is the mapping/query confidence split (library L2 #6) or +-12 px vantage jitter, not more distillation. (c) cosine stays < 0.4 at weight 5 -> the student cannot absorb the target; retry once with DISTILL_WEIGHT 20 and a wider projector before concluding anything. (d) training fails on the teacher download (torch.hub needs GitHub + dl.fbaipublicfiles.com from the AWS box; pip install already proves egress) -> infrastructure, not a verdict; rerun. Standing check: the score must move through usable_fix_rate; if it improves only through false_fix_rate with usable flat, the teacher taught honesty, not place, and that is still a kept improvement but rule (b) applies.
init_strategy: from-scratch (deployed student unchanged); training-only teacher pretrained:dinov2_vits14_reg (Apache-2.0, torch.hub facebookresearch/dinov2), never exported
eli5: We hired a tutor. A large, freely licensed vision model that has already looked at hundreds of millions of photographs describes a scene by its roads, buildings and water, not by the colour cast, the season or where the shadows fall. During training only, our tiny navigator is shown one survey's photo of a spot and asked to produce the description the tutor gives for a DIFFERENT survey's photo of that same spot, so anything that changes between surveys is useless to it and only the layout pays. A measurement on the three training surveys shows the tutor recognises a place across surveys even when the view is shifted 12 m, where raw pixels fail nine times out of ten. The tutor never flies: what stays on the drone is exactly the same small model as before, now trained to see the city the way the tutor does.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent small strided conv stacks (112 channels at the top), sharing no weights; each turns the frame into its own compact fingerprint. Unchanged at inference; during training its 8×8 map is also read by the tutor loss

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor feeds its own scorer over all ~3,000 128 m map tiles of Berlin; the two tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: besides its own tile-and-offset loss on a re-photographed view, each member's 8×8 feature map (through a throwaway adapter) must match what a frozen, freely licensed foundation model (DINOv2 ViT-S/14) says about the SAME spot in a DIFFERENT survey's photograph; the foundation model is a training-time tutor only and is discarded at export. Paired three-survey batches, re-photographing, targets, schedule and views per epoch unchanged.

implementation_brief:
Fixed contracts (unchanged, the frozen scorer depends on them): model/train.py CLI `python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`, writing <out>/models/<area>.onnx and appending to <out>/train_info.json; model/model.py's ONNX contract 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalised map coords, conf in [0,1], the whole decode inside the graph; exported ONNX <= 4 MiB (must read exactly 3,942,411 bytes as in experiment 7 — the deployed graph does not change); training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train') and NOTHING under model/ may open the eval capture (truedop_2024) in any form. Do NOT place any teacher weight file under model/ or anywhere in the repo: loop.sh quarantines files over MAX_COMMIT_MB=25 out of the kept commit, so an 88 MB checkpoint in model/pretrained/ would be silently removed; use torch.hub's own cache only (already populated on this laptop at ~/.cache/torch/hub by the design-stage probe; the AWS box downloads it fresh, it has outbound internet since its boot script pip-installs).

=== model/model.py ===
1. In class Member add
   def feature_map(self, x):
       """[B, chans[-1], 8, 8] conv map before global average pooling (read by the training-only distillation loss)."""
       return self.features(x)
   and rewrite forward() as `f = self.feature_map(x).mean(dim=(2, 3))` — identical computation, so the exported graph is byte-identical in structure.
2. Everything else (CellLocNet, block_mask, forward decode, loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position, N_MEMBERS=2, MEMBER_CHANS=[3,24,48,96,112], CELL_PX) stays untouched. Add a short docstring paragraph 'CROSS-SURVEY DINOv2 DISTILLATION (experiment 8)' stating that the teacher and projectors live only in train.py and never enter the export.

=== model/train.py ===
3. Constants, next to AUG:
   TEACHER_HUB = ('facebookresearch/dinov2', 'dinov2_vits14_reg')
   TEACHER_RES = 112        # 112/14 = 8 patch tokens per side == the student's 8x8 map
   TEACHER_DIM = 384
   PROJ_WIDTH = 512
   DISTILL_WEIGHT = 5.0
   IMAGENET_MEAN = (0.485, 0.456, 0.406); IMAGENET_STD = (0.229, 0.224, 0.225)
4. def load_teacher(device): t = torch.hub.load(*TEACHER_HUB, trust_repo=True); t.eval(); for p in t.parameters(): p.requires_grad_(False); return t.to(device). Print one line '[area] teacher dinov2_vits14_reg loaded, 22.1M params, frozen, res 112'. The hub code warns that xFormers is missing — harmless, do not install anything. On MPS keep fp32; on CUDA wrap teacher calls in torch.autocast('cuda', dtype=torch.float16).
5. def teacher_targets(teacher, x_clean, mean, std): x_clean is float [B,3,128,128] in [0,1] on the device (UNaugmented). y = F.interpolate(x_clean, size=(TEACHER_RES, TEACHER_RES), mode='bilinear', antialias=True, align_corners=False); y = (y - mean) / std; with torch.no_grad(): tok = teacher.forward_features(y)['x_norm_patchtokens'].float()  # [B, 64, 384]; t = tok.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, TEACHER_DIM, 8, 8); t = t - t.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)  # batch-centre: remove the common token component so the cosine is not vacuous (exp 3's lesson); return F.normalize(t, dim=1). mean/std are [1,3,1,1] tensors built once on the device.
6. Projectors (train-only, NOT part of the model, so export is unaffected): in train_area after build_model: projectors = nn.ModuleList(nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(MEMBER_CHANS[-1], PROJ_WIDTH, 1), nn.ReLU(inplace=True), nn.Conv2d(PROJ_WIDTH, TEACHER_DIM, 1)) for _ in range(N_MEMBERS)).to(device); build the optimiser over list(model.parameters()) + list(projectors.parameters()) (same Adam lr=1e-3, same cosine schedule). Pass projectors and the teacher into run_epoch.
7. run_epoch, inside the mini-batch loop, after xb0 is cut: partner capture index: if n_caps > 1: cap_p = (cap_b + torch.randint(1, n_caps, (B,), device=device)) % n_caps else cap_p = cap_b (generic single-capture areas distil from the same crop). xb_p = gpu_crops(scene, cap_p, cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx]) — SAME position and heading, different survey, clean. tgt = teacher_targets(teacher, xb_p, ...) once per batch (shared by both members). Then in the per-member loop replace `logits_k, off_k = member(xb_k)` with: fmap_k = member.feature_map(xb_k); f_k = fmap_k.mean(dim=(2, 3)); logits_k = member.cls_head(f_k); off_k = torch.tanh(member.off_head(f_k)) * 0.5 (identical to Member.forward); z_k = F.normalize(projectors[k](fmap_k), dim=1); cos_k = (z_k * tgt).sum(dim=1)  # [B,8,8]; distill_k = (1.0 - cos_k).mean(); loss = loss + loss_fn(logits_k, off_k, soft_t, off_t_k) + DISTILL_WEIGHT * distill_k. Keep the existing offset target, top1, member top1, agree-rate and mean_max_softmax bookkeeping exactly as they are. Add running device-side accumulators distill_sum[N_MEMBERS] (+= distill_k.detach() * B) and cos_sum[N_MEMBERS] (+= cos_k.detach().mean() * B); return them in the stats dict as 'distill' and 'cos' lists.
8. Epoch log line: append ' distill=[m0, m1] student_teacher_cos=[c0, c1]' (4 decimals), computed as the per-view means. train_info additions: 'distillation': {'teacher': 'dinov2_vits14_reg (torch.hub facebookresearch/dinov2, Apache-2.0)', 'teacher_res': 112, 'teacher_dim': 384, 'proj_width': 512, 'weight': DISTILL_WEIGHT, 'target': 'batch-centred L2-normalised patch tokens of the SAME position+heading in a DIFFERENT training capture (clean crop)', 'student_input': 'augmented own-survey crop'}, 'final_distill_loss': [..], 'final_student_teacher_cos': [..]; set 'init' to 'from-scratch (student); training-only teacher pretrained:dinov2_vits14_reg' and extend 'capture_sampling' with ', cross-survey DINOv2 patch distillation'. Keep every existing train_info key.
9. Memory/throughput: the teacher forward is under no_grad; on CUDA under fp16 autocast; batch size stays 64. Do not call .item()/.cpu() inside the step loop (device-side accumulators only). torch.hub.load prints download progress on first use; that is expected on the AWS box.
10. Update the train.py module docstring with a 'CROSS-SURVEY DINOv2 DISTILLATION (experiment 8)' paragraph: what the target is, why the partner is a different survey, why batch-centring, that teacher+projectors are discarded at export and that no weight file is kept in the repo.
